children: M&G's stock appears expensive but interim results suggest the company is on track to meet full-year forecasts, RBC Capital Markets analysts Ben Cohen and Sarah Chong write. The U.K. investment manager's first-half profit and capital generation were broadly in line with consensus and RBC forecasts, the analysts say. Despite guidance for low double-digit profit growth in 2026, M&G still expects 2% dividend growth. The company is expensive compared with peers on IFRS, capital generation and dividend yield bases, RBC notes. RBC maintains its sector perform recommendation and 335 pence price target on the stock. Shares closed at 330.80 pence on Tuesday. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)
